m.h:
The profit rate assumes 15 kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

200 killstreaks at Telos require the player to have extreme knowledge of Telos' mechanics, as a single mistake will most likely kill the player and lose a large portion of the loot, including all uniques in most cases. Completing a 200 killstreak comes with its own grandmaster combat achievement, which gives some idea of the challenge involved. For every successful kill in the streak you keep 5% of the quantity of each item if the streak is failed, up to a maximum of 75% at a streak of 15 or more. The number that is kept is rounded down, so if you have only 1 of an item, such as a very valuable dormant seren godbow, then the item is always lost.

The average 200 killstreak starts at 0% enrage, increases by 11.5% for every successful kill, and ends at around 2300% enrage. At 15 kills per hour, completing a 200 killstreak will take 13.3 hours. This guide averages over the duration of the streak, and assumes that no loot is lost due to a failed kill.

Uniques

The drop rate of uniques at telos starts at 1/1000, and increases by 1/1000 for every 40 enrage or 3.33 kills in the streak, with a cap of 1/15. This means that an average 200 killstreak should contain 9.603 uniques, which is an average drop rate of 1/20.83, however the drops will be weighted toward appearing later in the streak. This means that a 200 killstreak will give fewer uniques than 2449% claims, which has a consistent drop rate of 1/15 for uniques.

This guide uses the average drop rate of 1/20.83 to calculate quantity of unique items.

Commons

The quantity of commons at telos also increases with streak length, however the formula for this is less well understood. Data taken by Evil Lucario who performed 8 complete 200 killstreaks in August 2021 indicates that, if averaging over a 200 killstreak, the total quantity of items obtained is 15 times what would be achieved in the same number of claims kills. This agrees with data from obtained from the drop log project, which indicates that the ratio of the minimum to maximum quantity of each item is approximately 1 to 30. This means that the common drops increase linearly for a 1 × multiplier at the start of the streak, to a 30 × multiplier at the end of the streak. This common drop multiplier means that streaking at telos is less reliant on obtaining unique drops than performing claims at a fixed enrage.

This guide uses the average multiplier of 15 × the quantity of commons compared to claims.

Comparison to 2449

In comparison to claims at 2449% enrage, 200 Killstreaks gives -28% of the uniques but +1400% of the commons, and adds the risk of losing loot.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 18 chest loots per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

With the right skills and equipment, high-level players can loot nearly 18 Barrows chests per hour, resulting in a sizable profit. At higher levels one may use any combat style, although most of the brothers are weak to magic. For best results, a Barrows amulet should be used on the tomb of Akrisae. For faster chests at the cost of lower ROI, Barrows amulets can also be used on Karil and Ahrim.

If barrows amulets are not used, the recommended strategy is to use a strong non-channelled ability first, then when Akrisae prays against your combat style, use either Smash, Dragon Breath or Snipe to hit through the prayer and disable it, then finish Akrisae off while his prayer is disabled. Alternatively, Necromancy can dispatch Akrisae very easily since he is unable to use the Protect from Necromancy prayer, making him easy to kill even if your damage is lacking.

Players with access to Soul Split will not need food except in emergency situations. Healing via Soul Split when in combat will typically cover all damage taken from the brothers and crypt monsters, but it should be noted that food can be cheaper per trip than prayer potions depending on the amount of damage you take per encounter. All of the brothers may be easily dispatched with threshold abilities. It is recommended to bind or stun Dharok when he has approximately half health, as he is capable of dealing excess damage. If using melee, dual-wielding is recommended for use of Destroy. By quickly running between each crypt, it is possible to keep adrenaline up the entire time so that threshold abilities may be used on all of the brothers. While low-levelled players may need to switch combat styles to cater to individual brothers' weaknesses, players with chaotic or higher weaponry should only rarely miss against any of the brothers. Additionally, it is not necessary to kill the brothers in any particular order. The only difference is the amount of time spent running between each crypt, simply based on the distance between two successive brothers. Kill 6 brothers, skipping Linza, and enter the remaining brother's tunnel.

The starting room of the tunnels has only one operational door. Find this door, and navigate through the tunnels. There is no need to kill any of the creatures in the tunnel since killing all 7 brothers is enough to maximum your reward potential. The chest is located in the centre of the tunnels, and only one of the four adjacent rooms may be used to enter the centre room. It is recommended to run through the passageways connecting corner rooms until finding a door with an "open" option leading into the central room. This door will be locked by a puzzle, and incorrectly answering the puzzle will cause the door to lock and require you to navigate the tunnels again to find a new door.

While running through the tunnels, any of the brothers which have not been killed may spawn when a door is opened. If the brother is not Akrisae, kill him when he spawns, and continue through the maze. It is recommended that prayer renewal be active when running through the tunnels so that Soul Split may be used when killing this brother. Upon opening the chest, the brother whose tunnel you are in will spawn if he has not yet been killed. If this brother is Akrisae, do not fight him. Otherwise, kill this brother. Loot the chest, and teleport out using Drakan's medallion. This teleport cannot be used when in combat, so it is recommended to run behind the chest if being attacked by Akrisae or a crypt monster. Alternatively the War's Retreat Teleport spell can be used to leave, with a boss portal attuned to the Barrows providing a quick way to return.

Players who have unlocked War's Blessing 1 from completing a sufficient amount of Combat Mastery achievements will gain access to a special portal in the starting room of the tunnels which will take them directly to the central room, where you can face the final brother upon opening the chest before looting. This will drastically speed up the number kills one can do per hour.

Experienced players should be able to complete one loot in under 3 minutes, though this will vary based on equipment and skill levels. At this rate, approximately 18 chests per hour are likely. However, with the recommended inventory supplies, it is possible to continue looting chests for several hours as only a small portion of the supplies will have been consumed after 1 hour.

Other Notes

  • Killing Linza adds a 1-in-192 (0.52%) chance of receiving one of her items but does not affect other rewards in any way.
    • At current GE prices, this means each Linza kill is worth an average of (1/960) * (10787538 + 10309311 + 11111947 + 882995 + 1552599) gp
  • Killing all seven brothers is enough to maximize the reward potential, so killing creatures in the tunnels will not further increase your rewards.
  • For a full description of the reward calculation, see the official drop rates page.
  • While not documented on the official drops page, having tier 2 luck or higher will increase the likelihood of getting barrows items and the amulet of the forsaken .

Vorago's fight consists of 5 phases, each taking place in a different level of the cave, and each having their own mechanics and attacks. Vorago also possesses a special attack which determines how phase 3, 4, and 5 are fought. The special attack he uses lasts for one week, changing every Wednesday at 00:00 UTC.

Vorago can be fought in either a public or a private instance. Every player who accepts the fight challenge must survive a hit of 70% of their max health as typeless damage.

Players can teleport out of the arena once the fight has begun in case one of the other players end up dying or disconnecting. If the player disconnects while fighting Vorago (either from poor internet connection or intentionally closing the client), they will be removed from the fight almost immediately.

Roles

Each team consists of up to 3 general roles, as well as room for additional free DPS. The bomb tank is responsible for standing furthest from Vorago, causing bombs to be directed towards them. The base tank is responsible for holding aggression, while the TL5 climbs the northwestern wall in phase 1 and takes the 5th bleed on phase 2 (and sometimes phases 3 and/or 4).

The TL5 role can be merged into the bomb tank role, allowing for more challenging, but even more profitable sessions.

Strategies

Refer to the strategy page for more information on the boss fight for each rotation and more.
